
```{python}
import pandas as pd
from IPython.display import HTML
import charts
import stories

# COUNTRY is set by the page that includes this body (index, fr, de, uk, es).
NAME = charts.COUNTRY_NAMES[COUNTRY]
ADJ = charts.COUNTRY_ADJ[COUNTRY]

# The parquet tables accumulate every country and snapshot; this page reads
# its own country's latest snapshot.
facts = pd.read_parquet("data/policy_facts.parquet").query("country == @COUNTRY")
snapshots = sorted(facts["snapshot_date"].unique())
snapshot = snapshots[-1]
n_snapshots = len(snapshots)
latest = "country == @COUNTRY and snapshot_date == @snapshot"
df = facts.query("snapshot_date == @snapshot")
sig = pd.read_parquet("data/sector_signals.parquet").query(latest)
res = pd.read_parquet("data/reserved_domains.parquet").query(latest)


def as_table(t, filename):
    """Table view of a chart's data — same numbers, no hover needed, and
    downloadable as CSV."""
    return HTML(charts.table_html(t, filename))

n_domains = int(sig["n_domains"].sum())
# Every site has one row per crawler, so one crawler's rows count the sites.
one_crawler = df[df["crawler"] == df["crawler"].iloc[0]]
n_unobserved = int(one_crawler.loc[one_crawler["source"] == "unobservable", "n_domains"].sum())
n_observed = n_domains - n_unobserved
n_llms = int(sig["llms_hand"].sum() + sig["llms_generated"].sum())
llms_share = f"{100 * n_llms / n_domains:.1f}%"
n_sectors = df["sector"].nunique()
n_crawlers = df["crawler"].nunique()
snapshot_label = (f"snapshot {snapshot}" if n_snapshots == 1
                  else f"snapshot {n_snapshots} · {snapshot}")

# Prose that states a finding is computed from the data, so a country page
# can't carry another country's sentence. The headline is that country's own
# finding (stories.py), chosen against the latest rows of all five.
all_facts = charts.latest_rows("data/policy_facts.parquet")
all_sig = charts.latest_rows("data/sector_signals.parquet")
all_res = charts.latest_rows("data/reserved_domains.parquet")
story = stories.choose(COUNTRY, all_facts, all_sig, all_res)
hero_chart, hero_table, hero_file, hero_caption = stories.hero(story, df, sig, res)
top = charts.top_block_sector(df)
top_name = "the press" if top["sector"] == "news" else top["sector_label"].lower()
offer_lead = charts.top_offer_sector(sig)
n_reserved = len(res)
```

## Block {#block}

Sites keep AI crawlers out through **robots.txt** — a plain-text file that can
name a crawler and disallow paths. The chart above counts only the rules that
name GPTBot; where that happens is uneven, and `{python} top_name` is the outlier.

Crawler by crawler, the picture is the same one seen from the other side. Each
bar is one crawler and splits into how the `{python} n_observed` sites we could
read treat it: **blocked** at the root, **partial** (some paths off limits), or
**allowed**. `{python} n_unobserved` sites blocked our crawler or answered from
another site; they have no verdict and are left out. Every bar is a
whole, so the figures inside it are shares of sites, not counts — the counts are
in the tooltip and the table. Use the menus to slice by sector, or by whether a
rule *names the crawler* or comes from a catch-all `*`.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Offer {#offer}

The opposite move. **llms.txt** (a 2024 convention) is a Markdown file that
*offers* a curated view of a site to language models — "here is what to read
about us." `{python} n_llms` of `{python} n_domains` sites publish one,
**`{python} llms_share`**. `{python} offer_lead`

The chart below counts only those `{python} n_llms` publishers — not the whole sample — and
splits each sector's bar by where the file came from: ink for a hand-written
file, gray for a plugin default. That split is the question this section asks:
how much of the adoption was a decision rather than a side effect. Sector
sample sizes are in the table.

::: {.panel-tabset}


## Reserve {#reserve}

The legal one. Under EU copyright law (Directive 2019/790, Article 4), AI
companies may text-and-data-mine public content for training **unless the owner
reserves the right in a machine-readable form**. **TDMRep** is that reservation —
the only one of the three signals with legal weight in the EU.

```{python}
HTML(charts.reserve_stat(sig, res))
```

```{python}
if n_reserved <= charts.NAMED_LIST_MAX:
    display(HTML("<p>Every site that reserves, and the channel it signals through:</p>"))
    display(as_table(charts.reserve_table(res), "tdmrep-sites.csv"))
else:
    display(HTML(f"<p>{n_reserved} sites reserve: too many to list here. "
                 "By who they are and how they signal (a site can use more than "
                 "one channel):</p>"))
    display(HTML(charts.reserve_summary_table(res).to_html(
        index=False, classes="table table-sm", border=0)))
    display(HTML(charts.csv_link(charts.reserve_table(res), "tdmrep-sites.csv",
                                 f"Download all {n_reserved} sites (CSV)")))
```

## Method {#method}

**The sample.** `{python} n_domains` `{python} ADJ` websites, stratified across
`{python} n_sectors` sectors, drawn from hand-curated sector lists cross-checked
against the Tranco top-1M list for the country's domain; a national site on
another domain qualifies if it is aimed mainly at that country. Latest snapshot:
`{python} snapshot`. Each crawl is one snapshot, so the same measures can be
tracked over time; the five countries are set side by side on the
[comparison page](compare.html). The sampling rules are in
[`sample/METHOD.md`](https://github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census/blob/main/sample/METHOD.md).

**The three signals.** For every site we fetch and *validate* three files:

- **robots.txt**, parsed under RFC 9309 (longest-match, `Allow` wins ties). A
  crawler's verdict is **blocked** when the root path is denied, **partial**
  when only some paths are, **allowed** otherwise. A rule is *specific* when the
  site names the crawler, *wildcard* when it comes from a catch-all
  `User-agent: *`.
- **llms.txt**, a Markdown file offering content to models. *Hand-written* vs
  *plugin default* is inferred from generator signatures and near-duplicate
  detection across sites.
- **tdmrep.json / TDMRep**, the EU legal reservation, read through all three
  spec channels (a well-known file, HTTP headers, and HTML meta tags).

**Presence is validated, never assumed.** A `200 OK` proves nothing — many
servers answer 200 with an HTML page on any path. A file counts only if it is
structurally valid; soft-404s are excluded.

**Limits.** robots.txt measures *declared intent*, not crawler behaviour. The
CMS/plugin fingerprint is heuristic. "Not mentioned" is a default, not a
decision, and is kept separate from explicit permission throughout. Every fetch
runs from one Italian address, so sites that answer differently by country are
under-observed outside Italy; they count as not observable, not as allowed.

**Data & code.** `{python} n_crawlers` AI crawlers are tracked. The full pipeline
and the aggregated snapshot data are open:
[github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census](https://github.com/mxdangelo/aicrawl-census).
